source.title: Cancelling a queued execution starts another one above N8N_CONCURRENCY_PRODUCTION_LIMIT

source.body:
### Bug Description

When production concurrency control is enabled (`N8N_CONCURRENCY_PRODUCTION_LIMIT`), cancelling or deleting a **queued** execution causes the next queued execution to start immediately, even though all running slots are still occupied. The instance then runs more production executions than the configured limit. Each cancelled or deleted queued execution lets one more execution through, so the overshoot grows with the number of queued executions that are removed.

For example, with `N8N_CONCURRENCY_PRODUCTION_LIMIT=1`, one execution running and two queued, cancelling the first queued execution starts the second one straight away. Two executions are then running at the same time while the limit is 1.

**Cause**

[`ConcurrencyQueue.remove()`](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/5bd8e21ac6fa6a15d56671af962915758549d905/packages/cli/src/concurrency/concurrency-queue.ts#L44-L54) calls `resolveNext()` after taking the execution out of the queue:

```ts
remove(executionId: string) {
	const index = this.queue.findIndex((item) => item.executionId === executionId);
	if (index > -1) {
		this.queue.splice(index, 1);
		this.capacity++;
		this.resolveNext();
	}
}
```

A queued execution hasn't started, so removing it frees no running slot. Incrementing `capacity` is correct, because it returns the place the waiting execution had reserved. But `resolveNext()` should only run when a running execution finishes, as in `dequeue()`. Here it releases a waiting execution while every running slot is still taken.

This is reached through `ConcurrencyControlService.remove()`, which runs when a queued execution is stopped (`ExecutionService.stopInRegularMode()`) or when an execution with status `new` is deleted.

The existing unit test [`should limit concurrency`](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/5bd8e21ac6fa6a15d56671af962915758549d905/packages/cli/src/concurrency/__tests__/concurrency-queue.test.ts#L52-L56) uses a limit of 1, but after `queue.remove('4')` it expects executions 3 and 5 to both be `started`. That's two executions running at once, so the test currently asserts the incorrect behaviour.

I'd like to submit a fix: drop the `resolveNext()` call from `remove()`, correct the existing test, and add a regression test.

### To Reproduce

1. Start n8n in regular mode with `N8N_CONCURRENCY_PRODUCTION_LIMIT=1`.
2. Import this workflow and activate it (Webhook responding immediately, then a 30-second Wait):

<paste the workflow JSON from earlier inside a ```json block>

3. Trigger it three times at once:
   `for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s http://localhost:5678/webhook/concurrency-test & done`
4. In the workflow's Executions tab, confirm 1 execution is Running and 2 are Queued.
5. Cancel the older of the two queued executions.
6. The remaining queued execution starts immediately, while the first one is still running.

### Expected behavior

Cancelling or deleting a queued execution should only remove it from the queue. The remaining queued execution should stay queued until the running execution finishes, so the number of running production executions never exceeds `N8N_CONCURRENCY_PRODUCTION_LIMIT`.
